bugs: A 422 with an empty body stores the reason 'Warehouse rejected the shipping address: ' with nothing after the colon (cosmetic) (app/Services/Warehouse/WarehouseClient.php:35-37)
antipatterns: Adds a WarehouseClient service and two custom exceptions for a single HTTP call, which is somewhat more ceremony than the task needs (app/Services/Warehouse/*)
The 422 and 429 paths are signalled with exceptions only for the job to catch and turn back into control flow (app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:55-73)
The test reads the Timeout attribute through reflection and compares it against queue config, which tests configuration rather than behaviour (tests/Feature/OrderShipmentTest.php:312-317)
Adds an extra shipment_notified_at column that the spec did not ask for (justified, but it adds to the schema) (database/migrations/2026_11_07_000000_create_orders_table.php:20)
strengths: Uses Skip::when middleware ahead of RateLimited, so cancelled or unpaid orders never spend the shared 5/s budget. A comment notes that restoring a serialized model ignores soft deletes

Claims the email with a conditional update on shipment_notified_at and releases the claim if sending fails. This makes the email truly exactly-once, including after a crash between saving the reference and sending
markShipmentFailed has a whereNull(shipment_reference) guard, so a late failure never downgrades a shipment that was already sent
Other 4xx responses (401 and similar) fail permanently instead of hammering the partner, while 408 is retried

Uses modern attributes (Backoff, MaxExceptions, Timeout, DeleteWhenMissingModels, WithoutRelations), retryUntil, afterCommit dispatch, an Idempotency-Key header, connect and request timeouts, and caps Retry-After while also handling the HTTP-date form
markAsPaid claims the order with a conditional update, so it refuses already-paid or cancelled orders
Very thorough Pest suite (32 tests) using describe blocks and datasets, covering mail failure, sequence recovery, connection failure, the sync-queue failure path and mail rendering

bugs: If queueing the email throws after shipment_reference is saved, the retry returns early because the reference exists, so the customer never gets the email. This is at-most-once, not exactly-once, and a probe confirmed it (app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:47,69-75)

failed() overwrites shipment_status to failed unconditionally. A probe confirmed it downgrades an order that already has a reference and status sent, which could happen if the final attempt throws after saving (app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:78-84)

Other permanent 4xx responses (401/403/400) throw a RequestException and are retried up to MaxExceptions(8), hammering the partner with a bad token instead of surfacing the problem to ops immediately (app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:65)
antipatterns: WithoutOverlapping keyed per order is unnecessary ceremony, because markAsPaid already guarantees a single dispatch and every release consumes an attempt (app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:35)
rejectionReason chains ?? and ?: without parentheses, which is hard to read (app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:103)
The 429 release expression mixes a cast, ?: and min() inline (app/Jobs/SendOrderToWarehouse.php:54)

Tests call (new Job)->handle() directly without withFakeQueueInteractions in several places, and the test of the failed() path calls failed() by hand without going through the worker (tests/Feature/SendOrderToWarehouseTest.php:154-162)
strengths: Compact, readable job: the HTTP call is in a private method and the code reads naturally
markAsPaid claims the order with a conditional update, refreshes the model, dispatches afterCommit and returns a bool
On 422 it calls $this->fail() with a domain exception, so the reason flows through failed() and lands on the order
Uses queue attributes (Backoff, MaxExceptions, Timeout), retryUntil, a named RateLimiter shared across the account, an Idempotency-Key header and connect and request timeouts
The ShipmentCreated mailable is queued (ShouldQueue), keeping the job fast
Tests use withFakeQueueInteractions with assertReleased and assertFailedWith, plus preventStrayRequests

v.rationale:
Both implementations share the same core design: a conditional-update claim in markAsPaid, afterCommit dispatch, a named 5/s RateLimiter shared across the account, Retry-After handling on 429, backoff with retryUntil, and an Idempotency-Key header. Both check trashed(), which is needed because restoring a serialized model ignores soft deletes. All tests pass in both (impl-2: 16, impl-1: 32).

The probes separate them. In impl-2, if queueing the mail fails after the shipment reference is saved, the email is lost for good because the retry exits early. Its failed() also downgrades a shipment that was already sent, and permanent 4xx responses like 401 keep retrying. impl-1 handles all three: the email is claimed and released if sending fails, the failure update is guarded on a null reference, and non-408 client errors fail fast. It also uses Skip middleware so cancelled orders don't spend rate-limit budget.

impl-1's only issue is cosmetic: an empty-body 422 leaves a dangling colon in the reason. It has more ceremony (a service class and two exceptions), but its tests are much stronger. impl-2 is simpler but has real correctness gaps against the "exactly once" email requirement and the requirement to surface permanent errors to ops. So impl-1 ranks first.
